question_text: Why is the Bill Pugh Singleton implementation in Java considered superior to standard double-checked locking without volatile variables?

options.text: It uses operating system mutexes directly
It relies on class-loader initialization semantics to guarantee thread safety without explicit synchronization locks
It permits multiple distinct instances when memory pressure occurs

answer_explanation: The nested static helper class is loaded only when `getInstance()` is called. The JVM guarantees class initialization is atomic and thread-safe without synchronization overhead.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: The nested static helper class is loaded only when `getInstance()` is called. The JVM guarantees class initialization is atomic and thread-safe without synchronization overhead.
